text.p: These are the leading stories in the Serbian and Montenegrin press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- SERBIA -
POLITIKA

- Yugoslav parliament adopted a law on concessions granting use of natural resources to Yugoslavs and foreigners for a maximum of 30 years. It also adopted a communications law allowing for the separation of the post from telecommunications service in Serbia's PTT.
- Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic recieves representatives of the interior ministry on occasion of May 13 Security Day.
- European Union's trade preferences to Yugoslavia officially entered into force Tuesday with the publication of the text in the EU official gazette.
- A Czech national exhibition grouping ten firms is organised within the scope of the Belgrade technics fair to promote bilateral economic cooperation.
- Bigger foreign investments can only be expected through individual deals with Yugoslav firms, says director of Belgrade Foreign Trade Institute Radovan Kovacevic.
- Leader of Serbian Renewal Movement (SPO) Vuk Draskovic is opposed to extension of coalition Zajedno which was proposed by another coalition parner Zoran Djindjic.

- Serbia's radio and TV frequencies will soon be distributed but for a provisional period of up to one year until federal bodies identify all available frequencies, says Serbian information minister Radmila Milentijevic.
- Oil refinery in Srpski Brod in the Bosnian Serb republic was reopened Tuesday after six years.
NASA BORBA
- Health workers strike is continuing with 80 percent of health institutions in Belgrade closed. Protest in front of Serbian government planned for Thursday.
- Serbian government and Italian Stet reach agreement on sale of Serbian PTT according to which the Italian side would purchase 49 percent of the country's telephony, paper sources say.
- The Novi Sad Agriculture fair will group 1,800 exhibitors, 300 of whom will be foreign from some 30 countries, said fair director Dusan Manojlovic.
- The Democratic Party of Socialists of Montenegro will support Slobodan Milosevic's candidacy for president of Yugoslavia, said Montnegrin President Momir Bulatovic on Montenegro TV.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Workers of construction firm Komgrap demand suspension of extraordinary measures introduced two years ago and resignation of acting director Milorad Vranjanac.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Some 30 tonnes of dead fish floating on Palic lake are the result of high temperatures and increased decay of algae and grass, according to Subotica health protection institue.
BORBA

- In response to speech of U.S Charge d'affaires in Belgrade Richard Miles Yugoslav Left (JUL) official Aleksandar Vulin said Yugoslasvia is always ready to be a valuable partner but who will always be equal and never subordinate.
- MONTENEGRO-
POBJEDA
- The outer wall of sanctions limits our economic growth, said Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic in an interview to TV Montenegro.

- President of Montenegrin Constitutional Court Blagota Mitric denies participating in writing of the statute of the Democratic Party of Socialists except for the provision stipulating that the DPS main board approve the composition of government.

- Montenegrin parliament political and legislative committees at separate sessions unanimously adopted the draft law on the security council. The committees rejected the opposition draft on the establishment of a parliamentary commission for control of the security service.

- Montenegro's crime rate is dropping. In the first four months this year 2,474 criminal acts were registered which is 24.42 percent less than in the same period last year, said Montenegrin police minister Filip Vujanovic on occasion of May 13, Security Day.
- Surgery department of the Podgorica central hospital asks for resignation of health minister Miomir Mugosa. -- Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 43 05
